question: What was the preliminary Class A IPO price range per share, and what was its midpoint?
expected_location: PROSPECTUS COVER PAGE;Cover Page and Important Notice;D.1 Under which conditions and timetable can I invest in this security?
reference_answer: The preliminary range was $70.00–$78.00 per share, with a midpoint of $74.00. [US-PROSPECTUS, Prospectus Cover Page; also EU-PROSPECTUS]

question: In the preliminary base IPO, how many Class A shares were offered in total, and how many were offered by Anthropic versus selling stockholders?
expected_location: PROSPECTUS COVER PAGE
reference_answer: The base offering consisted of 825,000,000 Class A shares: 801,351,354 offered by Anthropic and 23,648,646 by selling stockholders. This excludes the overallotment option and the Class N private placement. [US-PROSPECTUS, Prospectus Cover Page]

question: For which purposes did Anthropic state it intended to use the net proceeds from the offering and the concurrent private placement, including the specified RSU tax-withholding obligation?
expected_location: USE OF PROCEEDS
reference_answer: The net proceeds from the offering and the concurrent private placement were intended for general corporate purposes, including working capital, operating expenses and capital expenditures (including investments in compute and infrastructure), and hiring and retention of highly skilled personnel; a portion could also be used to acquire or invest in businesses, products, services or technologies, although there were no agreements or commitments for material acquisitions. A portion was also intended to satisfy anticipated RSU Settlement tax withholding and remittance obligations of $3.8 billion, based on the assumed $74.00 midpoint price and an assumed 50.90% tax withholding rate. [US-PROSPECTUS, Use of Proceeds]

question: According to the preliminary Use of Proceeds sensitivity, approximately how much would combined net proceeds change if the assumed offering price rose or fell by $1.00 per share?
expected_location: USE OF PROCEEDS
reference_answer: The disclosed sensitivity for combined net proceeds from the offering and concurrent private placement was approximately +/−$793 million for a $1.00 change in the assumed offering price. [US-PROSPECTUS, Use of Proceeds]

question: At the $74.00 preliminary midpoint price, what was the estimated immediate dilution in net tangible book value per share for new IPO investors?
expected_location: DILUTION;8.8.2 Economic Dilution of Existing and New Shareholders
reference_answer: The estimated immediate dilution was $65.79 per share, based on a pro forma as adjusted net tangible book value of $8.21 per share as of September 30, 2026, at the $74.00 assumed offering price. [US-PROSPECTUS, Dilution]

question: How many additional Class A shares could the underwriters purchase under the preliminary overallotment option?
expected_location: PROSPECTUS COVER PAGE;8.4.2.2 Option to Purchase Additional Shares
reference_answer: The preliminary underwriters’ overallotment option covered up to 123,750,000 additional Class A shares. [US-PROSPECTUS, Prospectus Cover Page]

question: For non-founder directors, officers, and current and former employees and consultants, what events determined the end of their IPO lock-up period?
expected_location: SHARES ELIGIBLE FOR FUTURE SALE > Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements
reference_answer: Their lock-up ended upon the earlier of (x) 6:00 AM Eastern Time on the second full trading day immediately following the Q1 Earnings Release Date or (y) the close of trading on the 180th day after the date of the prospectus (or the last trading day before it, if the 180th day is not a trading day). [US-PROSPECTUS, Shares Eligible for Future Sale — Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements]

question: What director appointment and removal rights did the Long-Term Benefit Trust generally hold through Class T common stock?
expected_location: Election and Removal of Directors;Section 7.1 Board Size and Election of Directors
reference_answer: The LTBT generally had the power to elect and remove Class T directors, who constituted a majority of the board. [US-PROSPECTUS, Election and Removal of Directors; CHARTER, Section 7.1]

question: What aggregate voting power did the Class F common stock held by the Founder LLC carry on matters submitted to stockholders generally before the Class F Sunset Time?
expected_location: DESCRIPTION OF CAPITAL STOCK > Common Stock > Voting Rights;Founder Voting Structure
reference_answer: The single share of Class F common stock, held by the Founder LLC (whose members are the co-founders), carried an aggregate number of votes equal to 50.1% of the total voting power of the outstanding capital stock on matters submitted to stockholders generally, until the Class F Sunset Time. This is voting power, not economic ownership. [US-PROSPECTUS, Description of Capital Stock — Voting Rights; Founder Voting Structure]

question: What specific public benefit does Anthropic’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation state that the corporation will promote?
expected_location: Article III;PROSPECTUS COVER PAGE
reference_answer: Article III states that the specific public benefit the corporation will promote is “to responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.” [CHARTER, Article III]

question: Which nine EEA countries were covered by the European retail offering, and was Switzerland part of that nine-country group?
expected_location: Cover Page and Important Notice;A. Introduction and Warnings
reference_answer: Germany, Denmark, Finland, France, Ireland, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, and Sweden were the nine Covered EEA Countries. Switzerland was addressed separately and was not part of those nine. [EU-PROSPECTUS, Cover / Introduction]

question: In the European retail offering, who decided how Class A shares were allotted to retail investors, and why could allocations differ between investors?
expected_location: 8.2.1 Plan of Allotment
reference_answer: Orders were subject to receipt and acceptance and to the underwriters’ right to reject any order in whole or in part at their discretion. This discretionary allocation could result in financial intermediaries receiving different allocations, and each intermediary could apply its own allocation principles to its clients, so the allocations received by retail investors in the European and Swiss retail offerings could differ. [EU-PROSPECTUS, Section 8.2.1 Plan of Allotment]

question: As of September 30, 2026, how many customers generated $1 million or more of revenue for Anthropic on a trailing-twelve-month (TTM) basis?
expected_location: Enterprise Adoption of Claude;MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS > Adoption of Claude
reference_answer: More than 1,900 customers had $1 million or more of revenue on a TTM basis as of September 30, 2026 (and approximately 250 had $10 million or more). [US-PROSPECTUS, Prospectus Summary — Enterprise Adoption of Claude; MD&A — Adoption of Claude]

question: What pricing mechanism generated the substantial majority of Anthropic’s revenue?
expected_location: How We Generate Revenue
reference_answer: The substantial majority of revenue came from pay-for-intelligence consumption-based pricing, notably usage measured in tokens. [US-PROSPECTUS, How We Generate Revenue]

question: Which major cloud providers did Anthropic identify in its concentration-of-CSPs risk disclosure, and what conflict-of-interest concern accompanied these dependencies?
expected_location: Our reliance on a limited number of CSPs and suppliers
reference_answer: Anthropic named Amazon, Google and Microsoft as the cloud service providers (CSPs) it relies on, and Broadcom as a supplier of compute and critical components of its compute infrastructure (a supplier, not a CSP). Some of these CSPs and suppliers have strategic and investment relationships with Anthropic and are also its customers, which creates complex dynamics that could give rise to conflicts of interest and adversely affect its access to compute. [US-PROSPECTUS, Risk Factors — Our reliance on a limited number of CSPs and suppliers]

question: For how much did Anthropic agree to settle the Bartz copyright class action, and when was the settlement agreement reached and approved by the court?
expected_location: We have been, are currently defending against
reference_answer: In September 2025, Anthropic reached an agreement to settle the copyright infringement class action Bartz, et al. v. Anthropic PBC for $1.5 billion; the settlement was approved by the district court in July 2026. [US-PROSPECTUS, Risk Factors — “We have been, are currently defending against, and may in the future be subject to, intellectual property claims…”]

question: For the full fiscal year 2025 (not the nine months ended September 2025), what were Anthropic’s revenue and net loss, in USD millions?
expected_location: CONSOLIDATED STATEMENTS OF OPERATIONS;PROSPECTUS SUMMARY > Consolidated Statements of Operations Data
reference_answer: For full fiscal 2025, revenue was $4,585 million and net loss was $41,965 million (shown as $(41,965) million). [US-PROSPECTUS, Consolidated Statements of Operations]

question: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, what Adjusted Operating Margin (non-GAAP) and what GAAP operating margin did Anthropic disclose?
expected_location: PROSPECTUS SUMMARY > Non-GAAP Financial Measures;MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS > Non-GAAP Financial Measures
reference_answer: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Adjusted Operating Margin (a non-GAAP measure) was 12%, compared with a GAAP operating margin of (4)%. [US-PROSPECTUS, Non-GAAP Financial Measures]

question: What maximum per-share price was specified in the European retail offering documentation?
expected_location: Cover Page and Important Notice;D.1 Under which conditions and timetable can I invest in this security?;8.1.3 Pricing
reference_answer: The European documentation stated a maximum price of $120.00 per share. This was a ceiling, not the preliminary expected offering range or the final IPO price. [EU-PROSPECTUS, Cover / D.1 / Section 8.1.3]

question: What aspects of the EU prospectus did BaFin approval cover, and what did that approval not imply?
expected_location: Cover Page and Important Notice;A. Introduction and Warnings;2.3 Competent Authority Approval
reference_answer: BaFin’s approval concerned the document’s completeness, comprehensibility and consistency; it did not constitute an endorsement of Anthropic or of the securities. [EU-PROSPECTUS, Section 2.3 Competent Authority Approval]

question: For whom was Class E common stock intended, and what voting and economic rights did that class have?
expected_location: PROSPECTUS COVER PAGE;C.1 What are the main features of the securities?
reference_answer: Class E was intended for employees other than the co-founders; it carried limited voting rights and no economic rights, as described in the preliminary documents. [US-PROSPECTUS, Cover; EU-PROSPECTUS, C.1]

question: What constituted a quorum of Anthropic’s board under Section 8.7 of the charter?
expected_location: Section 8.7 Board Quorum
reference_answer: A majority of the Whole Board, including at least one At-Large Director, was required; the charter also described a reconvening mechanism after at least 48 hours. [CHARTER, Section 8.7 Board Quorum]

question: Which US retail brokerage channels were identified for IPO share sales, and which investors were eligible for the European retail tranche?
expected_location: Sales to Retail Investors;8.1.1 Eligible Retail Investors|D.1 Under which conditions and timetable can I invest in this security?
reference_answer: US retail channels included Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood, SoFi and E*TRADE, among others. The European retail tranche was restricted to retail investors — persons or entities that do not qualify as qualified investors under the Prospectus Regulation — resident or located in one of the Covered EEA Countries. [US-PROSPECTUS, Sales to Retail Investors; EU-PROSPECTUS, Section 8.1.1 / D.1]

question: Which strategic investors were named in Anthropic’s $26.0 billion concurrent Class N private placement, and were those shares subject to the IPO lock-up?
expected_location: CONCURRENT PRIVATE PLACEMENT;SHARES ELIGIBLE FOR FUTURE SALE > Concurrent Private Placement Shares
reference_answer: Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC were named as participants in the approximately $26.0 billion Class N private placement. Those shares were not subject to the IPO lock-up, although resale was subject to restrictions including Rule 144. [US-PROSPECTUS, Concurrent Private Placement; Shares Eligible for Future Sale — Concurrent Private Placement Shares]

question: At the assumed $74.00 price, what were the estimated net proceeds from the offering and the concurrent private placement, and what were the reported total contractual obligations and the type of expense accounting for most of them?
expected_location: USE OF PROCEEDS;Contractual Obligations
reference_answer: Estimated net proceeds from the offering and the concurrent private placement were approximately $84.6 billion at the assumed $74.00 midpoint price (approximately $93.7 billion if the underwriters’ option is exercised in full). Contractual obligations were approximately $900.9 billion, substantially all related to compute and infrastructure; payments under other compute and infrastructure arrangements without a fixed dollar commitment (estimated at $150–175 billion) were excluded from that amount. [US-PROSPECTUS, Use of Proceeds; MD&A — Contractual Obligations]

question: Which chip platforms did Anthropic describe in its multi-chip compute strategy, and what separate risk did it disclose about relying on cloud service providers?
expected_location: Multi-Chip Compute Approach;Our reliance on a limited number of CSPs and suppliers
reference_answer: The strategy mentioned AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs and AMD GPUs. A separate risk disclosure described Anthropic’s reliance on a limited number of cloud service providers. [US-PROSPECTUS, Multi-Chip Compute Approach; Risk Factors — Reliance on CSPs]

question: What quarterly minimum liquidity covenant applied to Anthropic’s revolving credit agreement beginning in Q4 2026, and what cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments did it report at September 30, 2026?
expected_location: Revolving Credit Agreement;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk
reference_answer: The A&R Credit Agreement required Anthropic to maintain liquidity of at least $5.0 billion as of the last day of each fiscal quarter, beginning with the fiscal quarter ending December 31, 2026. As of September 30, 2026, Anthropic reported $95.6 billion of cash and cash equivalents and $36.3 billion of short-term investments; these amounts should not automatically be treated as the covenant-defined liquidity measure. [US-PROSPECTUS, MD&A — Revolving Credit Agreement; Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk]

question: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, what share of revenue came from Anthropic’s five largest customers and what was total revenue over that period?
expected_location: A substantial portion of our revenue and accounts receivable is driven by a limited number of customers;CONSOLIDATED STATEMENTS OF OPERATIONS|PROSPECTUS SUMMARY > Consolidated Statements of Operations Data
reference_answer: The five largest customers represented approximately 25% of revenue, with no single customer exceeding 10%; total revenue for the nine-month period was $33,242 million. [US-PROSPECTUS, Customer Concentration Risk; Statements of Operations]

question: What IPO lock-up milestone applied to Anthropic’s co-founders, and what distinct conditions could trigger the Class F voting-power sunset?
expected_location: SHARES ELIGIBLE FOR FUTURE SALE > Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements;Sunset Provisions
reference_answer: Co-founders’ lock-up: it ended upon the earlier of (x) 6:00 AM Eastern Time on the second full trading day immediately following the Q3 Earnings Release Date or (y) the close of trading on the 365th day after the date of the prospectus, subject to timed automatic expirations. Class F Sunset Time: it occurs on the earlier of (i) the time when no Class F common stock remains outstanding (including through redemption agreed by a Supermajority of the Continuing Founders or upon dissolution of the Founder LLC) and (ii) completion of the Class F Transition Period, which commences when there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders for 90 consecutive calendar days. [US-PROSPECTUS, Shares Eligible for Future Sale — Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements; Our Governance Structure — Sunset Provisions]
